Status: variant parameters for T-35 (docs/research/refurbished-hardware.md); exploration, not used by any scored figure
Description: Expected failure (wear) cost per 1 kW server-year and work-per-kWh factors. Read by scripts/refurbished_comparison.py. Kept outside config/hardware/*.json on purpose: HardwareProfile.LoadDirectory only reads the top-level profile files. Formula: wear CHF per server-year = sum over parts of n_parts x AFR_base x k_age x k_temp x k_cycle x (part replacement price + repair hours x labour CHF/h).

GpuAnnualFailureRate.source: TrendForce 2024-10-31 (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2024/10/31/news-datacenter-gpus-may-have-an-astonishingly-short-lifespan-of-only-1-to-3-years), annualised from Meta's Llama 3 405B run: 148 GPU + 72 HBM3 interruptions on 16,384 H100 in 54 days (tomshardware.com, datacenterdynamics.com); own check 220 / 16384 x 365 / 54 = 0.091. Interruptions, not all replacements; 700 W training GPUs at full load: an upper bound for 70 W inference cards (search snippets, accessed 2026-11-21, medium)

ServerRepairsPerServerYear.source: Vishwanath and Nagappan, Characterizing Cloud Computing Hardware Reliability, SoCC 2010 (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/characterizing-cloud-computing-hardware-reliability/): 8 % of servers saw a hardware repair, those averaged 2 repairs; 70-78 % of repairs are hard disks; observation window treated as one year (TODO(source): exact window from the full paper; snippets, medium)

GpuRepairHours.source: assumption: swap one PCIe card in a water-cooled host, incl. test; TODO(source)

ServerRepairHours.source: assumption: disk, PSU or DIMM swap incl. travel within a city; TODO(source)

ServerRepairPartShareOfUnitPrice.source: assumption: average replaced part (mostly disks, per Vishwanath 2010) costs 10 % of the server; TODO(source)

AgeFactorRefurbished.source: assumption, sensitivity 1-3: hardware 3-7 years old. Evidence is qualitative: Backblaze drive stats show a flat failure rate for most of the life, then a wear-out rise (https://www.backblaze.com/blog/backblaze-drive-stats-for-2025/); Vishwanath 2010: a server that failed once is likely to fail again; TrendForce: GPUs fail more often after a year of heavy use. No published GPU failure rate by age found, TODO(source)

HotWaterTemperatureFactor.source: assumption, sensitivity 2: water at 50-65 C keeps dies near the 70-85 C of air-cooled datacentre GPUs, and steady liquid cooling was reported to halve board failures at LRZ SuperMUC (https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/analysis/getting-into-hot-water/, unverified claim). Sensitivity 2 = Arrhenius factor for a die 10 K hotter at about 75 C with Ea 0.7 eV (common default activation energy, TODO(source))

ThermalCycleFactor.source: derived: Coffin-Manson N_f(dT) = N_ref x (dT_ref / dT)^n with N_ref = 4,535 cycles at 0/100 C (CBGA 361 example, https://corpora.tika.apache.org/base/docs/govdocs1/549/549854.pdf via snippet, low), n = 1.9 (Norris-Landzberg SnPb; 2.65 for SAC, https://e2e.ti.com/support/data-converters-group/data-converters/f/data-converters-forum/730473/solder-joint-reliability-acceleration-model); at dT = 60 K N_f = 11,950 cycles. Reference-house hourly run (data/derived/reference-house-v1) has 39 whole-server starts per year for 4 servers (9.75 per server), using 0.08 % of fatigue life per year: negligible. Factor 1 holds only if the scheduler limits starts to about 1 per day (3 % of fatigue life per year); hourly on/off (8,760 per year) would use 73 % per year

WorkPerKwhRelativeToReference.source: SPECpower_ssj2008 overall ssj_ops/W: 6,006 (2 x Xeon Gold 6226R, Cascade Lake Refresh, spec.org/power_ssj2008/results/res2022q2) / 20,408 (2 x Xeon Platinum 8592+, spec.org/power_ssj2008/results/res2024q2); snippets, configurations not matched, low
same chip; assumption: no throughput loss with age for a cooled card, TODO(source)
